l.i: Cùm ergo victor simul & victus utrinque
plectar, dones me geminata Spiritus tui[?] portio-
ne, & ea gratiæ mensura quæ mihi sola sufficiat.
Quemadmodum me habuisti miserrimum, ita
maxime facias reformari; ut non solum eò fœlix
sim, ut civilium dissidiorum finem videam, sed
Instrumentum etiam fiam præcipuum reddituræ
Pacis,*& in Regnis meis fœliciter stabiliendæ.
Sit diversarum Partium una æmulatio, ut se
invicem ratione, & moderatione animi exsupe-
rent, & ea postremo sui abnegatione, quæ deceat
illos qui cogitant mutuis nostris dissidiis scindi
publicum, & id Bonis maxime expedire ut fit
omnium concordia.
Sin Tu (Domine) qui ob peccata nostra ca-
lamitates Belli induxisti, pergas adhuc ob pec-
cata Belli fœlicitatem Pacis denegare, & nos
usque detinere in calamitatum circulo, des Mihi
tamen Famulo Tuo & fidelibus meis (licet op-
pressis) Subditis ea tandem pace frui[?], quam nec
Mundus dare potest, nec eripere.
Ne Mihi sanguinem Subditorum meorum im-
pu-averis[?], animo valde reluctanti, & dolore
summo effusi in illa justa mea & necessaria de-
fensione, sed me pretioso illo lava Sanguine, à
Magno illo Pacificatore Iesu Christo propter
Me effuso, quem Me brevi confido ex his omni-
bus angustiis liberaturum: novi enim Iubila-
tionem Impiorum brevem esse, & gaudium Hy-
pocritæ ad instar puncti.

page.notes: Printed number "20." at the foot right, beside the catchword "De", is uncertain and not transcribed. A small bullet (•) follows "puncti." and is an ornament, not transcribed. The mark after "tui" looks like a semicolon or comma; marked [?]. "impu-averis": the letter after "impu-" looks like a faint t; marked [?]. "frui" is marked [?] because the final letter is unclear. "effuso" and "lava" are read from a small, slightly blurred print. The star after "Pacis," is printed. "Cùm ergo" opens the page without an indent, so the first paragraph is marked as a continuation.
